title: Programming Languages and Frameworks
answer: The languages AI is written in and the frameworks built on top of them, tracked by adoption, releases, licence, and integrations.

reading.body:
The software layer of AI is organized into three parts: languages, frameworks, and inference engines.

That split is the useful signal here. Languages are where models and training code are written. Frameworks sit above them and shape how applications are assembled. Inference engines sit below the application and decide how cheaply a trained model can actually be served. The three are stacked, not parallel, and each layer constrains the one above it.

For AI specifically, the inference layer is where software meets the physical constraint. Serving efficiency determines how much of a given accelerator, and therefore how much power and building capacity, is needed per unit of output. A faster engine is a substitute for hardware at the margin. The data names vLLM, TensorRT, and llama.cpp as that serving layer but gives no benchmarks, so the size of that substitution cannot be read from it.

What this does not cover: there are no adoption numbers, release dates, licence terms, or integration counts, despite the summary saying those are tracked. The entry is a map of the category, not a measurement of it. Nothing here supports a claim about which language or framework is winning, or by how much.
